parts.gloss: even that which one is skilled in

words.gloss: even that which one is truly skilled in

literal: Behaving by undertaking things not learned, even that which one is thoroughly skilled in will bring doubt.
translation: Pretending to practice what one has not learned will cast doubt even on the things one is truly skilled in.
modern: தான் கற்காதவற்றை அறிந்தவர் போல மேற்கொண்டு நடப்பது, ஒருவன் குற்றமறக் கற்றுத் தேர்ந்தவற்றின் மீதும் மற்றவர்களுக்கு ஐயத்தை உண்டாக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the folly of pretending to possess knowledge or skills that one has not actually learned. When a person falsely undertakes tasks beyond their knowledge, they expose their ignorance. This pretense is so damaging that it ruins their overall credibility. Consequently, even in fields where they are genuinely and flawlessly skilled, others will begin to look upon them with doubt and suspicion.
